$comment: Single source of truth for fork-only patches that upstream main does NOT carry. Consumed by scripts/check-fork-only-patches.mjs (wired into `pnpm check`). See docs/fork-only-patches.md. Every develop_base rebuild from upstream main MUST re-apply these; the guard turns a silent loss into a red check.
$baselineComment: The pre-rebuild tip, read straight out of git. `git reset --hard upstream/main` replaces the working tree but does NOT move remote-tracking refs, so this ref still holds the previous tree's registry - and this guard - after a rebuild has erased both from disk. Run the guard as the last step of a rebuild to compare what the previous tree claimed to protect against what the new one actually has. NOT fork/optimizations: that branch is an orphan July snapshot (7 commits, no merge-base with upstream/main), so membership of it is not a survival predicate.

patches.why: Skips scheduled eval-cat invocation when the domain's evidence source cannot produce evidence (OTel disabled). Without it every daily eval:a2a fire burns a full LLM session to re-conclude a known gap.
patches.upstreamStatus: rejected-as-fork-scope (zts212653/clowder-ai#1352 closed 2026-08-25; issue #1353 accepted the direction then closed as fork-specific)

requiredAnchors.note: execute-path ordering: the evidence gate must run BEFORE publishPrereqProbe, or it cannot prevent the invocation it exists to prevent. Anchored on CALL SITES, not bare symbols - imports and interface fields would satisfy a substring check while the executed gate was gone.

patches.why: The guard that detects every other entry's loss. Its develop_base workflow is the only automatic enforcement point: all other workflows in this repo trigger on `main`, and develop_base is the branch rebuilt onto upstream main. Lose this and the guard degrades to 'someone remembers to run pnpm check' - the exact failure mode it replaces.
patches.upstreamStatus: fork-scope by construction - upstream has no develop_base branch and carries none of these patches

requiredAnchors.note: the trigger that makes the guard automatic; a workflow that survives with a main-only trigger is silently inert
local enforcement: wired FIRST in `check` so a rebuild fails fast; definition + chain wiring are separate revert cases
